lines.text: Don't make me leave and go where promises, hearts,
spectrums of light-filled constellations are broken.
I escaped here for a reason,
believing this would give me a sharpened key of answers
in a more grounded bravado
for my life of conquests and queries.
The way you see things felt safe and timeless.
Whatever has terminated this moment, damn you,
but let it feel love and lost as we must endure,
absent artificial escapes and machine learning strengths
for my highs and lows as resource materials.
Well, I can't leave behind the impulse
that comes from battle scars
and can't leave behind the wisdom that brushes gray tones
into our melanin after disappointments and defeats.
I trust that you'll be fine.
I escaped here for a reason.
Our dance together is a victory to entwine muses,
immersed in twisted dons for a hot minute,
and a genesis of a New Testament as it ends.

scenes.lines: (won't prevent me / from sharing / a smile worth / the promise of my heart.) A hot minute. The haze gathers on the water — and everything I built here learns to be weather: the city, the temple, the harbor.
scenes.treatment: Haze gathers on water, over harbor, and grows. Atlantis, the new temple and the harbor all slowly become haze.

shots.action: haze gathers low on the water and grows; POET small on the quay, back to us, watching it come

bodies.action: watches the haze rise off the water

shots.action: the haze climbs over the city towers, the white temple and the pier until all of it is weather; only a roofline, the temple eave and the pier arm stay as faint traces
the last trace: the temple's eave line hangs in the haze, then goes

scenes.lines: Don't make me leave / & go where / promises— ... (It takes me last, and from the ground up. I am reluctant — but I have been weather before.)
scenes.treatment: Haze slowly envelopes POET from ground up body, who is reluctant at first. [reference: Lawrence Raab, "Walking Alone"]

shots.action: the haze takes POET last, from the feet up: he stands with arms half open, swaying, as it climbs past his knees

bodies.action: stands as the haze climbs his legs, arms half open

shots.action: reluctant: the haze holds at his chest for a long beat; his jaw sets, then softens
the haze finishes: his head goes last and he is weather

bodies.action: lifts his chin as the haze closes over him

scenes.lines: whatever has terminated / this moment / damn you. but / let it feel love / & loss as we must endure— (All black again. But no walls this time.)
scenes.treatment: POET is floating again in all black.

shots.action: all black, one open horizon of faint light; POET floats in it, drifting slowly across the frame
floating close: a slow rise and fall like breath, nothing around him

scenes.lines: absent artificial escapes / & machine learned / strengths / from our highs / & lows / as sourced materials— ... (A life flashes the way a reel does: the window, the tambourine, the field, the stars, the candle, the daisy, the ride, the temple, the hourglass.)
scenes.treatment: Cut back and forth from POET floating to B-Roll scenes of life. Human scenes that capture the highs and lows of life. Cut back and forth from POET floating in blackness.

shots.action: the reel, first four exposures with black frame-lines between them: the window, the tambourine, the field, the stars
cut back: POET floating in blackness, eyes now open, watching his life go by
B-roll human scenes, highs and lows: someone laughing in a crowd, someone grieving with head in hands

bodies.action: laughs with arms up in a crowd

shots.action: the reel speeds up: the candle, the daisy, the ride, the temple, the hourglass, each flash shorter than the last

scenes.lines: I trust that / you'll be fine / I escaped here for a / reason. / our dance together / is a victory— / two entwined muses / immersed in / twisted dawns / for a hot minute—
scenes.treatment: POET still floating in all black. Old vintage door appears.

shots.action: in the black, two figures of POET hold hands and turn around each other on a faint ring of floor; far behind them an old vintage door has appeared, warm light under it

bodies.action: turns with his double, reaching hand in hand
turns with POET, reaching hand in hand

shots.action: entwined: the spin slows into a landing; both raise their arms together, victory

scenes.lines: with growth that'd / last forever, / as it ends. (An old door, from a vintage somewhere. It opens on a slow party — the kind I once fell out of a window to escape. This time, I choose the door.)
scenes.treatment: POET enters through door into old-time vintage party, guests are in romantic slow-motion. POET disappears into crowd from back. Door closes. END.

shots.action: POET walks through the black to the old door and opens it; warm light spills out across him

bodies.action: walks to the door and turns the knob

shots.action: inside: an old-time party, couples dancing cheek to cheek in romantic slow motion under the garland; the window on the wall stays shut

bodies.action: slow-dances, holding a coupe behind his partner

shots.action: POET walks away from us into the slow-motion crowd and disappears among the dancers
the door closes on the light; black. END.

passage.line: I trust that you'll be fine.
passage.why_fulcrum: The one line that releases EX: 'Don't make me leave' becomes a blessing, so the door that follows is chosen, not fled to, and the dance and the loop read as letting go.

answer.title: Don't Be Afraid
answer.said: Someone you're fond of and trust.
answer.why: His trust is answered with who it is placed in: someone you're fond of. Same sense of trust, tender; the film's title also echoes his calm.

passage.gesture: a hand that opens and stays open
passage.gesture_detail: Right hand, loosely closed at his side, opens palm-up toward the door as he speaks and stays open through the answer.
passage.surface: the doorway of the old vintage door that materializes in the black, opened a hand's width then wider

plate.why: Floating in the black; scene 14.4 has the vintage door materialize in this same all-black space, so the doorway is the one surface that belongs there.

passage.staging: Black void, POET floating left of center; an old door draws itself in to his right; the archive picture fills the doorway; warm light spills on his cut-out.
